messages:
Jamie Lin: Quick question — I'm going to split the Terraform state for k8s overlays so dev/staging/prod each have their own backend (mainly to use different KMS keys & separate promote windows). Plan shows a couple secrets moving under new paths. Has anyone run into issues when the secret path prefix changes for our k8s-secret-manager wiring? e.g. old: /redwood/staging/foo -> new: /env/staging/foo

Lina Patel: You can do it, but watch the kustomize overlays + the secret controller mapping. If we change the path key names, the controller won't auto-swap unless the mapping file in staging overlay is updated. Also check the RBAC for the SA reading the new KMS key :eyes:

Mike R.: Also watch rotation. If we duplicate paths then rotate one copy, apps reading the old path might still succeed until we flip them. We had a silent issue once where an app cached the secret for 15m and the rollout looked green but later failed under load. Suggest a short TTL refresh during the cutover. :thumbsup:

Alex Zhao: My recommended sequence: 1) create new secret copies under new prefix, 2) update apps to read new path behind a feature flag, 3) flip a small canary subset, 4) monitor, 5) delete old. Keeps traffic steady and allows rollback.

Jamie Lin: That matches what I was thinking. Two small things: do we prefer SSM parameter store or Secrets Manager for the overlay consumer? And how do we wire TF so promote pipeline doesn't attempt to delete+recreate resources across envs?

Lina Patel: We standardize on Secrets Manager for secrets that KMS-protect and require rotation. SSM for non-secret flags. For TF, treat each env as separate workspace/backends and *don't* move resources between states — instead import into the target state after creating duplicates. The promote pipeline should run a "plan-only" on staging then an apply on prod only after manual approval.

Mike R.: To avoid accidental delete, add a preflight check in CI that compares resource counts/ids between states and blocks destroy-heavy plans. Also add a tag-based guard in TF to refuse changes that move resource between prefixes without explicit override.

Alex Zhao: Example backend snippet I used recently (simplified):
```
terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket = "redwood-tfstate"
    key    = "envs/staging/k8s-overlay.tfstate"
    region = "us-west-2"
    kms_key_id = "arn:aws:kms:...:alias/redwood-staging"
  }
}
```
And for secrets import we did: `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version` + `kubernetes_secret` resource mapping.

sre-oncall: reminder — any change that touches secret paths or KMS needs an incident runbook update. Also the release gating should include a live traffic canary + auto-fallback if >5% errors for 5 minutes. We'll add that to the pipeline template.

deploy-bot: TF plan for branch env/split-secret-paths (commit 3f5a2): 
```
Plan: +7 to add, ~2 to change, -0 to destroy
No drift detected.
```

Jamie Lin: OK thanks team. I'll: create duplicates, open a PR with the new backend + mapping changes, add the CI preflight, and request a canary deploy. Ping me if you want to review the PR (will post link when it's up). :raised_hands:

Lina Patel: Ping me on the PR, I'll review the kustomize overlay changes.

Mike R.: I'll take the CI preflight hook review.

Alex Zhao: Happy to help with the canary job config.

sre-oncall: I'll update the runbook and add the gating thresholds to the pipeline template.

Jamie Lin: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412 — includes backend split + secret copy script. TL;DR in PR body.

Lina Patel: Reviewing now. Looks sane at a glance. :eyes:

deploy-bot: apply scheduled to staging after manual approval.
